Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 39, verse 1–3:

Surat az-Zumar (The Companies)

Meccan, except for His saying ﴿Say, O My servants who have transgressed against themselves﴾ and the verse that follows it. [[Al-Nahhas narrated in his History, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: "The surah az-Zumar was revealed in Mecca, except for three verses which were revealed in Medina concerning Wahshi, the slayer of Hamzah: ﴿Say, O My servants who have transgressed against themselves﴾, up to three verses." See also: Zad al-Masir, 7/160.]] In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

﴿The revelation of the Book is from Allah﴾ [i.e., this is the revelation of the Book from Allah. And it is said: "The revelation of the Book"] [[What is between the brackets is an addition from manuscript "B".]] is the subject (mubtada'), and its predicate is: ﴿from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise﴾, meaning: the revelation of the Book is from Allah and not from anyone else.

﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth﴾. Muqatil said: "We did not send it down as something vain, for no purpose," ﴿so worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion﴾, meaning in obedience.

﴿Unquestionably, to Allah belongs the pure religion﴾. Qatadah said: it is the testimony that there is no deity except Allah. And it is said: [No one deserves the pure religion except Allah. And it is said: the pure religion, free of shirk, belongs to Allah.] [[In manuscript "A": "No one deserves the pure religion free of shirk except Allah."]]

﴿And those who take protectors besides Him﴾, meaning besides Allah, ﴿[as protectors]﴾, meaning: the idols, ﴿"We worship them only that they may bring us nearer to Allah in position."﴾ That is how Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Abbas recited it.

Qatadah said: That is because when they were asked, "Who is your Lord, and who created you, and who created the heavens and the earth?" they would say, "Allah." Then it would be said to them, "What, then, is the meaning of your worship of the idols?" They would say, "They bring us nearer to Allah in position," i.e., nearness. The word zulfa is used in the place of a verbal noun, as if he said: "only that they may bring us near to Allah in nearness, and intercede for us with Allah." ﴿Indeed, Allah will judge between them﴾ on the Day of Resurrection ﴿concerning that over which they differ﴾ regarding matters of religion. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a liar and a disbeliever﴾, meaning He does not guide to His religion the one who lies, who says that the deities will intercede, and the taking of deities besides Him is sufficient as a lie [and as disbelief]. [[Omitted in manuscript "B".]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 39, verse 4–6:

﴿If Allah had desired to take a son, He would have chosen﴾ (i.e., He would have chosen) ﴿whatever He wills from what He creates.﴾ That is: the angels, as He said: "If We had desired to take a diversion, We would have taken it from Our presence" [al-Anbiya: 17]. Then He declared Himself free of that, saying: ﴿Glory be to Him﴾, exalting Him above that and above whatever is unworthy of His purity. ﴿He is Allah, the One, the Subduer.﴾

﴿He created the heavens and the earth in truth. He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night.﴾ Qatadah said: He covers this over that, as He said: "He covers the night with the day" [al-A'raf: 54]. It was also said: He makes one of them enter upon the other, as He said: "He makes the night enter into the day and makes the day enter into the night" [al-Hajj: 61].

Al-Hasan and al-Kalbi said: He reduces from the night and adds to the day, and reduces from the day and adds to the night. What is reduced from the night enters the day, and what is reduced from the day enters the night. The maximum reduction is nine hours, and the maximum increase is fifteen hours. The root meaning of al-takwir (wrapping) is to wind and gather, and from it comes the expression "kawwara al-'imamah" (he wound the turban).

﴿He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running for an appointed term. Unquestionably, He is the Mighty, the Forgiving.﴾

﴿He created you from a single soul﴾ — that is, Adam — ﴿then made from it its mate﴾ — that is, Hawwa' (Eve) — ﴿and He sent down for you from the cattle﴾ — the meaning of "sending down" here is bringing into existence and creating, as in His saying: ﴿We have sent down to you clothing to cover your private parts﴾ [al-A'raf: 26].

It was also said: He sent down the water, which is the cause of the growth of cotton from which clothing is made, and the cause of the growth of the plants by which the cattle are sustained.

It was also said: "and He sent down for you from the cattle" means He made them a provision and sustenance for you.

﴿Eight pairs﴾ — kinds. Its explanation is in Surah al-An'am [see above: 3/196-197]. ﴿He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation﴾ — a drop, then a clinging clot, then a lump of flesh, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And He has created you in stages﴾ [Nuh: 14]. ﴿In three darknesses﴾ — Ibn 'Abbas said: the darkness of the belly, the darkness of the womb, and the darkness of the amniotic sac [see: al-Tabari: 23/196; al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/212]. ﴿That is Allah﴾ — who created these things — ﴿your Lord; His is the dominion. There is no god but Him, so how are you turned away?﴾ — from the path of truth after this clarification.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 39, verse 7–8:

﴿If you disbelieve, then indeed Allah is Free of need from you. And He does not approve disbelief for His servants.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Suddi said: He does not approve disbelief for His believing servants, and they are those about whom Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, My servants, you have no authority over them﴾ [al-Hijr: 42]. So it is general in wording but specific in meaning, like His saying: ﴿A spring from which the servants of Allah drink﴾ [al-Insan: 6], meaning some of the servants. Others took it as general and said: He does not approve disbelief for any of His servants.

The meaning of the verse is: He does not approve that His servants disbelieve in Him. This is narrated from Qatadah, and it is the saying of the early scholars (al-salaf). They said: the disbelief of the disbeliever is not pleasing to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, even though it occurs by His will.

﴿And if you are grateful﴾ — you believe in your Lord and obey Him — ﴿He approves it for you﴾, so He rewards you for it. Abu ʿAmr recited "yarḍahu lakum" with the ha' silent (sakinat al-ha'), while the people of Madinah, ʿAsim and Hamzah pronounce it with a brief vowel (yakhtalisuha), and the rest pronounce it with a full elongated vowel (bi'l-ishbaʿ).

﴿And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you of what you used to do. Indeed, He is Knowing of the contents of the breasts.﴾

﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon his Lord, turning to Him in repentance﴾ — returning to Him, seeking His aid — ﴿then when He grants him a favor from Himself﴾ — He gives him a blessing from Himself — ﴿he forgets﴾ — he abandons ﴿what he had been calling to Him for before﴾, i.e., he forgets the harm which he had been calling on Allah to remove. ﴿And he sets up rivals to Allah﴾ — meaning the idols — ﴿to mislead from His way﴾ — to make others slip from the religion of Allah.

﴿Say﴾ to this disbeliever: ﴿Enjoy your disbelief for a little while; indeed, you are of the companions of the Fire.﴾ It was said: it was revealed concerning ʿUtbah ibn Rabiʿah. Muqatil said: it was revealed concerning Abu Hudhayfah ibn al-Mughirah al-Makhzumi. And it was said: it is general for every disbeliever. [[See: Zad al-Masir: 7/165.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 39, verse 9:

﴿Is he who is devoutly obedient﴾ Ibn Kathir, Nafi' and Hamzah read "Amman" with the mim lightened (takhfif), while the others read it with the mim doubled (tashdid). Whoever doubles it has two possible readings:

The first: the mim in "amm" is a particle of connection (silah), so the sense of the speech is interrogative and its answer is omitted. Its implied meaning is: "Is he who is devoutly obedient like him who is not devoutly obedient?" Compare His saying: ﴿Is he whose breast Allah has opened to Islam...﴾ [al-Zumar: 22], meaning: like him whose breast has not been opened.

The other reading: it is coordinated (atf) upon the interrogative, its implied meaning being: "He who has set up rivals to Allah, is that better, or he who is devoutly obedient?" Whoever reads it lightened, the alif is an interrogative alif that has entered upon "man", meaning: "Is this one like him who has set up rivals to Allah?"

It is also said: the alif in "aman" carries the meaning of the vocative particle, its estimated form being: "O you who are devoutly obedient," for the Arabs address with the alif just as they address with the ya', so they say: "abani fulan" and "ya bani fulan." The meaning of the verse then is: "Say: enjoy your disbelief for a little while; indeed you are among the companions of the Fire. O you who are devoutly obedient ﴿in the watches of the night﴾, indeed you are among the people of Paradise." This was said by Ibn 'Abbas.

In a narration from 'Ata': it was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq. [[Mentioned by al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 426.]]

Al-Dahhak said: it was revealed concerning Abu Bakr and 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both. [[See: al-Bahr al-Muhit: 7/419.]]

And from Ibn 'Umar: it was revealed concerning 'Uthman. [[Mentioned by al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 426.]]

And from al-Kalbi: it was revealed concerning Ibn Mas'ud, 'Ammar and Salman.

Al-qanit (the devoutly obedient) is one who persists in obedience. Ibn 'Umar said: "al-qunut" is the recitation of the Qur'an and prolonged standing. "Ana' al-layl" are its hours. ﴿Prostrating and standing﴾ means: in prayer. ﴿Fearing the Hereafter﴾ means: fearing the Hereafter. ﴿And hoping for the mercy of his Lord﴾ means: [the verse contrasts him] with one who does none of that. ﴿Say: Are those who know equal to those who do not know?﴾ It has been said: "those who know" refers to 'Ammar, and "those who do not know" refers to Abu Hudhayfah al-Makhzumi. ﴿Only those of understanding remember.﴾

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 39, verse 10:**

﴿Say: O My servants who believe, fear your Lord.﴾ By obeying Him and avoiding disobeying Him. ﴿For those who do good in this world, there is good.﴾ That is, those who believe and do good deeds. ﴿Good﴾ means Paradise, as Muqatil said. Al-Suddi said: "The good in this world" means health and well-being. ﴿And Allah's earth is spacious.﴾ Ibn Abbas said: it means leave Makkah. This verse encourages emigration (hijrah) from a land where sins are openly committed.

It was also said: it was revealed concerning the emigrants to Abyssinia.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: whoever is commanded to commit sins should flee.

﴿Indeed, the patient will be given their reward without account.﴾ Those who were patient in their religion and did not abandon it because of harm.

It was also said: it was revealed concerning Ja'far ibn Abi Talib and his companions, who did not abandon their religion when trials intensified upon them, and they were patient and emigrated. [[See: al-Bahr al-Muhit: 7/419.]]

Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Every obedient person is measured out to with a measure and weighed out with a weight, except the patient, for they are poured out upon in handfuls." [[See: al-Qurtubi: 15/241.]]

It is also narrated: "The people of trials will be brought forward, no scale will be set up for them and no record will be spread out for them, and reward will be poured upon them in a flood without account." [[A fragment of a hadith attributed by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/215 to Ibn Mardawayh.]] Allah the Exalted said: (﴿Indeed, the patient will be given their reward without account﴾), to the point that the people of ease in this world will wish that their bodies were cut with scissors, because of the virtue that the people of trials will receive.

**[Surah 39, verses 11–20]**

﴿Say: "Indeed, I have been commanded to worship Allah, making religion sincerely His."﴾ *Mukhlisan lahu al-din*: making the Oneness (*al-tawhid*) sincerely His, "I do not associate anything with Him."

﴿And I have been commanded to be the first of the Muslims.﴾ Of this *ummah* (community).

﴿Say: "Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord,"﴾ and worship other than Him, ﴿"the punishment of a great Day."﴾ This was said when he was called to the religion of his fathers.

﴿Say: "It is Allah I worship, making my religion sincerely His. So worship what you will besides Him."﴾ This is a command of rebuke and threat, like His saying: "Do what you will" [Fussilat: 40]. ﴿Say: "Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families,"﴾ meaning their wives and servants, ﴿"on the Day of Resurrection."﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: This is because Allah has made for every person a dwelling in Paradise and a family. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 39, verse 21–22:

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky, and makes it flow through springs in the earth?﴾ He made that water enter (yanabi') [[Plural, its singular is (rakiyah), which is a well.]] ﴿springs﴾, meaning streams, and wells ﴿in the earth﴾. Al-Sha'bi said: Every water in the earth has come down from the sky. ﴿Then He brings forth by it﴾, i.e., by the water, ﴿crops of varying colours﴾: red, yellow and green. ﴿Then it dries up﴾, i.e., withers, ﴿and you see it turn yellow﴾ after its greenness and freshness, ﴿then He makes it into debris﴾, crushed and broken pieces. ﴿Indeed in that is a reminder for those of understanding.﴾

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿So is one whose breast Allah has expanded to Islam﴾, widened it to accept the truth, ﴿and he is upon a light from his Lord?﴾ He is not like one whose heart Allah has hardened.

Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Shurayhi informed us, Abu Ishaq Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tha'labi informed us, Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Shayba narrated to us, Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Yazid al-Mawsili narrated to us in Baghdad, Abu Farwa, whose name is Yazid ibn Muhammad, narrated to us, my father narrated to me from his father, Zayd ibn Abi Unaysa narrated to us, from Amr ibn Murra, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: (So is one whose breast Allah has expanded to Islam, and he is upon a light from his Lord). We said: O Messenger of Allah, how is the expansion of the breast? He said: "When the light enters the heart, it expands and widens." We said: O Messenger of Allah, what is the sign of that? He said: "Turning to the abode of eternity, withdrawing from the abode of deception, and preparing for death before death comes." [[Al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur 7/219 as narrated by Ibn Mardawayh, and Hafiz Ibn Hajar cited it in al-Kafi al-Shafi p. 143 as narrated by al-Tha'labi, al-Hakim and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab, from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud. He said: "In its chain is Abu Farwa al-Rahawi, about whom there is some criticism. It was also narrated by al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi in al-Nawadir in the Sixth-Eighty-First Section (al-asl al-sadis wa'l-thamanin)."]]

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿So woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of Allah. Those are in manifest error.﴾ Malik ibn Dinar said: No servant has been afflicted with a punishment greater than hardness of heart, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has not become angry with a people except that He has removed mercy from them. [[Cited by al-Qurtubi: 15/248.]]

God Almighty says: ﴿Allah has sent down the best of speech, a Book whose parts resemble one another﴾. Its parts resemble one another in excellence, and some parts confirm others, with no contradiction or discrepancy in it.

﴿Oft-repeated﴾: in it the mention of promise and threat, command and prohibition, reports and rulings is repeated. ﴿Whose skins shiver﴾: they tremble and recoil. ﴿At it the skins of those who fear their Lord shiver﴾. Least al-iqshi'rar (shivering) is a change in a person's skin at times of dread and fear. It has also been said that what is meant by "skins" is the hearts, that is, the hearts of those who fear their Lord. ﴿Then their skins and their hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah﴾, that is, at the remembrance of Allah. That is, when verses of punishment are recited, the skins of those who fear Allah shiver, and when verses of mercy are recited, their hearts soften and become calm, as Allah Most High says: ﴿Surely in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest﴾ [al-Ra'd: 28].

The real meaning is that their hearts shiver from fear and soften in hope.

Abu Sa'id al-Shurayhi informed us, Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us, al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed me, Musa ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Abdus ibn Kamil narrated to us, Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Hamid al-Himmani narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Yazid ibn al-Had, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Taymi, from Umm Kulthum daughter of al-'Abbas, from al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the skin of a servant shivers from the fear of Allah, his sins fall away from him as the leaves fall from a dry tree." She said: "They were as Allah Almighty described them: their eyes shed tears and their skins shiver." He said: I said to her: "Today there are people who, when the Qur'an is recited to them, one of them falls down unconscious." She said: "I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan." [[al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (7/222) to Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn 'Asakir. al-Qurtubi also mentioned it (15/249).]]

And with the same chain, [Sulayman ibn] [[Omitted from "b".]] Salamah narrated to us, Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, Sa'id ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Jumahi narrated to us, that Ibn 'Umar said: He passed by a man from the people of Iraq who had fallen down. He said: "What is wrong with this man?" They said: "When the Qur'an is recited to him, or when he hears the remembrance of Allah, he falls down." Ibn 'Umar said: "We fear Allah, yet we do not fall down!"

It is related from Ibn Sirin: "Those who are struck down when the Qur'an is recited to them?" [He said: "Between us and them is this: let one of them sit on the roof of a house with his legs stretched out, then let the Qur'an be recited to him from its beginning to its end. If he throws himself down, then he is truthful."] [[What is between the parentheses is omitted from "a".]] [[Mentioned by the author of al-Bahr al-Muhit (7/423) and by al-Qurtubi (15/249).]]

﴿That﴾ refers to the best of speech. ﴿It is the guidance of Allah, by which He guides whom He wills, and whoever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 39, verse 24–28:

﴿Is he then who shields with his face from the evil of the punishment﴾ — that is, its severity — ﴿on the Day of Resurrection﴾. Mujahid said: he will be dragged on his face in the Fire. ʿAtaʾ said: he will be thrown into the Fire upside down, so the first thing the Fire touches of him is his face. Muqatil said: it means that the disbeliever is thrown into the Fire with his hands chained to his neck, and on his neck is a rock like a great mountain of sulphur. The Fire will ignite the stone, and it hangs from his neck; he falls down with its blaze on his face, unable to push it away from his face because of the shackles on his neck and hand [[These sayings are mentioned by al-Qurtubi: 15/251.]].

The meaning of the verse is: Is he who shields with his face from the evil of the punishment like one who is safe from the punishment?

﴿And it will be said﴾, that is, the keepers of Hell will say, ﴿to the wrongdoers: Taste what you used to earn﴾, that is, its consequence.

﴿Those before them denied﴾, before the disbelievers of Makkah, they denied the messengers, ﴿so the punishment came upon them from where they did not perceive﴾, that is, while they were secure and heedless of the punishment.

﴿So Allah made them taste disgrace﴾, the punishment and humiliation, ﴿in the life of this world; but the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if only they knew﴾.

﴿And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur'an every kind of example, that perhaps they will remember﴾, that is, that they may take heed.

﴿An Arabic Qur'an﴾, it is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (ḥāl), ﴿without any crookedness﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: without contradiction. Mujahid said: without confusion. al-Suddi said: not created. This is narrated from Malik ibn Anas, and it is related from Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna, from seventy of the Successors (tabiʿin), that the Qur'an is neither creator nor created [[These sayings are mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/223–224.]] ﴿that perhaps they will be mindful of God﴾, that is, of disbelief and denying it.

﴿Say: "To Allah belongs all intercession."﴾ Mujahid said: No one intercedes except by His permission. ﴿"To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. Then to Him you will be returned."﴾

﴿When Allah alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter shrink﴾ meaning they are repelled. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and Muqatil said: they contract from monotheism. Qatada said: they become arrogant. The root meaning of *ishmi'zaz* (shrinking with aversion) is aversion and arrogance. ﴿...and when those other than Him are mentioned, behold, they rejoice﴾ meaning they are glad. Mujahid and Muqatil said: This occurred when the Prophet ﷺ recited Surah al-Najm, and Satan cast into his recitation: "Those are the exalted cranes (gharaniq al-'ula)," and the disbelievers rejoiced at it. [[See above in the commentary on Surat al-Hajj, verse (52): 5/394, note (1).]]

﴿Say: "O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You judge between Your servants concerning that over which they used to differ."﴾

Abu 'Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi informed us; Abu Nu'aym al-Isfara'ini informed us; Abu 'Awana informed us; al-Sulami narrated to us; al-Nadr ibn Muhammad narrated to us; 'Ikrima ibn 'Ammar narrated to us; Yahya ibn Abi Kathir informed us; Abu Salama narrated to us, saying: I asked 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, with what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to begin the prayer at night? She said: He would say: "O Allah, Lord of Jibril, Mika'il and Israfil, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You judge between Your servants concerning that over which they used to differ. Guide me, by Your permission, to the truth regarding that over which they differed, for You guide whom You will to a straight path." [[Narrated by Muslim in the book of the Prayer of Travellers, chapter: Supplication in the night prayer and its standing, no. (770), 1/534; and the author in *Sharh al-Sunnah*: 4/71.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 39, verses 47–50:

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And if those who did wrong possessed whatever is on the earth entirely and the like of it with it, they would surely ransom themselves therewith from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection. And there will appear to them from Allah that which they had not been reckoning.﴾ Muqatil said: there will become apparent to them, when they are resurrected, what they had not reckoned in the world, that it would descend upon them in the Hereafter. As-Suddi said: they thought that [their deeds] were good deeds, but then they appeared to them as evil deeds. The meaning is that they used to draw near to Allah by worshipping idols, and when they were punished for it, there appeared to them from Allah what they had not reckoned. It is related that Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir became distressed at death, and when he was asked about that he said: "I fear that there will appear to me what I had not reckoned." [See: al-Qurtubi: 15/265–266.]

﴿And there will appear to them the evils of what they earned﴾, i.e., the bad consequences of their deeds, from associating partners with Allah and from wronging the friends of Allah.

﴿And there will befall them what they used to mock at.﴾

﴿So when harm touches a man, he calls upon Us; then when We bestow upon him a favor from Us, he says, "I was only given it because of knowledge."﴾ Harm: hardship. ﴿Bestow﴾: give. ﴿Because of knowledge﴾, i.e., because of knowledge from Allah that he is deserving of it. Muqatil said: "because of a good that Allah knows is in me." He used the pronoun in the singular because the intended meaning of "favor" is the act of bestowing. ﴿Rather, it is a trial﴾ [meaning: that favor is a trial], a respite from Allah the Exalted, a test and an affliction. It was also said: "Rather, his saying it is a trial."

﴿But most of them do not know﴾ that it is a respite and a test.

﴿Those before them had already said it﴾. Muqatil said: this refers to Qarun, for he said: "I was only given it because of knowledge I have" [al-Qasas: 78]. ﴿So what they used to earn did not avail them﴾: their disbelief did not avail them anything against the punishment.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 39, verses 51–53:**

﴿So the evil deeds they had earned befell them.﴾ That is, their recompense, which is the punishment. Then He threatened the disbelievers of Makkah, saying: ﴿And those who have wronged among these, the evil deeds they earned will befall them, and they cannot escape.﴾ That is, they cannot get away, because their return is to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿Do they not know that Allah extends provision to whom He wills?﴾ That is, He widens provision for whom He wills, ﴿and restricts it﴾ for whom He wills. ﴿Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe.﴾

The saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah."﴾

Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that some people of polytheism had killed and killed much, and committed adultery and committed it much. They came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "What you call to is indeed good, if only you would tell us that there is an expiation for what we have done." So this verse was revealed. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, Tafsir of Surah az-Zumar, chapter: "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves..." (verse 53), 8/549.]]

ʿAtaʾ ibn Abi Rabah narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent to Wahshi, inviting him to Islam. He sent back: "How do you invite me to your religion, when you claim that whoever kills, or associates partners with Allah, or commits adultery, will meet a penalty, and the punishment will be doubled for him, and I have done all of that?" So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "Except one who repents, believes, and does righteous deeds" [Maryam: 60]. Wahshi said: "This is a harsh condition; perhaps I will not be able to do it. Is there anything other than this?" So Allah, Exalted, revealed: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [an-Nisa: 48, 116]. Wahshi said: "I still see myself in doubt, so I do not know whether He will forgive me or not." So Allah, Exalted, revealed: "Say, O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah." Wahshi said: "Yes, this is it." So he came and embraced Islam. The Muslims said: "Is this specific to him, or is it general for the Muslims?" He said: "Rather, it is general for the Muslims." [[Al-Suyuti cited it in ad-Durr al-Manthur 7/235 as narrated by at-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman, with a weak chain. al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id 7/101: "At-Tabarani narrated it in al-Awsat, and in its chain is Abin ibn Sufyan, whom adh-Dhahabi declared weak." Ibn 'Adi and Ibn Hibban and others also declared him weak.]]

It is narrated from Ibn ʿUmar that he said: These verses were revealed concerning ʿAyyash ibn Abi Rabiʿah, al-Walid ibn al-Walid, and a group of Muslims who had embraced Islam but then were tested and tortured, so they wavered. We used to say: "Allah will never accept from these people any repentance or ransom, ever. A people who embraced Islam and then abandoned their religion because of a torment they were subjected to." So Allah, Exalted, revealed these verses. ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab wrote them with his own hand, then sent them to ʿAyyash ibn Rabiʿah, al-Walid ibn al-Walid, and those men. They embraced Islam and emigrated. [[Narrated by at-Tabari 24/15. See also al-Wahidi, Asbab al-Nuzul, pp. 427–428.]]

Muqatil ibn Hayyan narrated from Nafiʿ from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: We, the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), used to see, or say: "Nothing of our good deeds is rejected, all of them are accepted," until the verse was revealed: "Obey Allah and obey the Messenger, and do not nullify your deeds" [Muhammad: 33]. When this verse was revealed we said: "What is this that nullifies our deeds?" We said: "The major sins and the grave immoralities." He said: So whenever we saw someone who had committed any of them, we said: "He has perished." Then this verse was revealed, so we refrained from speaking about that. So whenever we saw anyone who had committed any of them, we feared for him, and if he had not committed any of them, we hoped for him. And by "transgression" (al-israf) he meant committing major sins. [[Narrated by at-Tabari 24/16.]]

It is narrated from Ibn Masʿud that he entered the mosque and found a storyteller telling stories and mentioning the Fire and the chains. He stood over his head and said: "O preacher, why do you make people despair?" Then he recited: "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah." [[Narrated by at-Tabari 24/16. Al-Suyuti cited it in ad-Durr al-Manthur 7/237 as narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi al-Dunya, Ibn Abi Hatim, at-Tabarani, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman.]]

Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Haytham at-Turabi informed us; Abu Muhammad ʿAbdullah ibn Ahmad al-Hamawi informed us; Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Khuzaym ash-Shashi informed us; ʿAbdullah [in B: ʿAbd al-Rahman] ibn Humayd narrated to us; Hayyan ibn Hilal, Sulayman ibn Harb and Hajjaj ibn Minhal narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us from Thabit, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Asma bint Yazid, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed Allah forgives all sins," and He does not mind. [[Narrated by at-Tirmidhi in Tafsir Surah az-Zumar 9/111–112, who said: "This is a good, gharib hadith; we do not know it except from the hadith of Thabit from Shahr ibn Hawshab." Also by the author in Shar al-Sunnah 14/384.]]

ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us; Ahmad ibn ʿAbdullah al-Nuʿaymi informed us; Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us; Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Abi ʿAdi narrated to us from Shuʿbah, from Qatadah, from Abu al-Siddiq an-Naji, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Among the Children of Israel there was a man who had killed ninety-nine people. Then he went out seeking (knowledge), and came to a monk and asked him. He said: 'Is there any repentance for me?' He said: 'No.' So he killed him, completing a hundred with him. Then a man said to him: 'Go to such-and-such a town.' Death overtook him on the way, so he leaned his chest toward it. The angels of mercy and the angels of punishment disputed over him. Allah, Exalted, revealed to this (land): 'Come closer,' and revealed to that (land): 'Move away,' and said: 'Measure what is between them.' It was found that he was a span closer to that (town), so he was forgiven." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Ahadith al-Anbiya' 6/512.]]

Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj narrated it from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna al-ʿAnazi, from [107b] Muʿadh ibn Hisham, from his father, from Qatadah with this chain, and he said: "He was directed to a monk, and he came to him and said: 'He has killed ninety-nine souls; is there any repentance for him?' He said to him: 'No.' So he killed him and completed a hundred with him. Then he asked about the most knowledgeable people on earth, and was directed to a learned man. He said to him: 'I have killed a hundred souls; is there any repentance for me?' He said: 'Yes, and who can come between him and repentance? Go to such-and-such a land, for there are people there who worship Allah, so worship Allah with them, and do not return to your land, for it is a land of evil.' So he set out, and when he was halfway, death came to him. The angels of mercy and the angels of punishment disputed over him. A angel in the form of a human came to them and they made him the judge between them. He said: 'Measure the distance between the two lands; whichever of them he is nearer to, he belongs to it.' They measured and found that he was nearer to the land he had intended, so the angels of mercy took him." [[Narrated by Muslim in at-Tawbah, chapter: "Acceptance of the repentance of a killer, even if his killings were many," no. 2766, 4/2118.]]

Abu al-Hasan as-Sarakhsi informed us; Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us; Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn ʿAbd al-Samad al-Hashimi informed us; Abu Musʿab informed us, from Malik, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-Aʿraj, from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A man, who had never done a good deed at all, said to his family when he died: 'Burn me, then scatter half of my ashes on land and half in the sea. By Allah, if Allah has power over me, He will punish me with a punishment that He has not inflicted on anyone among the worlds.' When he died, they did as he commanded. So Allah commanded the sea and it gathered what was in it, and commanded the land and it gathered what was in it. Then He said to him: 'Why did you do this?' He said: 'Out of fear of You, O Lord, and You know best.' So He forgave him." [[Narrated by Malik in al-Muwatta' 1/240; al-Bukhari in at-Tawhid, chapter: "(They wish to change the words of Allah)" 13/466; Muslim in at-Tawbah, chapter on the vastness of Allah's mercy and that it precedes His wrath, no. 2756, 4/2109–2110; and the author in Shar al-Sunnah 14/380.]]

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn ʿAbdullah ibn Abi Tawbah informed us; Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Harith informed us; Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Yaʿqub al-Kisa'i informed us; ʿAbdullah ibn Mahmud informed us; Ibrahim ibn ʿAbdullah al-Khallal informed us; ʿAbdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us from ʿIkrimah ibn ʿAmmar, who narrated to us Damdam ibn Jaws, who said: I entered the mosque of Madinah, and an old man called out to me, saying: "O Yamani, come here!" I did not know him. He said: "Do not say to a man: 'By Allah, Allah will never forgive you, and Allah will not admit you to Paradise.'" I said: "And who are you, may Allah have mercy on you?" He said: "Abu Hurayrah." I said: "Indeed, one of us says this word to some of his family when he is angry, or to his wife, or to his servant." He said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Two men among the Children of Israel were loving friends; one of them strove diligently in worship, and the other seemed to be a sinner. He kept saying: "Stop, stop from what you are doing." He would say: "Leave me alone with my Lord." Until one day he found him committing a sin that he considered grave, and said: "Stop!" He said: "Leave me alone with my Lord. Were you sent to watch over me?" He said: "By Allah, Allah will never forgive you, and will never admit you to Paradise." So Allah sent to them both an angel, who took their souls. They gathered before Him, and He said to the sinner: "Enter Paradise by My mercy." And He said to the other: "Can you prevent My servant from My mercy?" He said: "No, my Lord." He said: "Take him to the Fire.'" Abu Hurayrah said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, he spoke a word that ruined his worldly life and his Hereafter." [[Narrated by Ibn al-Mubarak in az-Zuhd, no. 900; Abu Dawud in al-Adab, chapter on the prohibition of oppression, 7/224–225; Ahmad 2/323; and the author in Shar al-Sunnah 14/384–385.]]

The saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, He is the Oft-Forgiving, the Most Merciful.﴾

ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr al-Qaffal informed us; Abu Mas'ud Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yunus al-Khatib informed us; Muhammad ibn Yaʿqub al-Asamm narrated to us; Abu Qilabah narrated to us; Abu ʿAsim narrated to us; Zakariyya ibn Ishaq narrated to us from ʿAmr ibn Dinar, from ʿAta', from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning the saying of Allah, Exalted: ﴿except for minor faults﴾ [an-Najm: 32]. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If You forgive, O Allah, You forgive much... and which servant of Yours does not commit faults?" [[Narrated by at-Tirmidhi in Tafsir Surah an-Najm, 9/172, who said: "This is a good, sahih, gharib hadith; we do not know it except from the hadith of Zakariyya ibn Ishaq." Also by the author in Shar al-Sunnah 14/387.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 39, verses 54–55:

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿And turn penitently to your Lord⦆ — approach and return to Him in obedience. ﴿And submit to Him⦆ — make tawhid (monotheism) sincere for Him, ﴿before there comes upon you the punishment, [after which] you will not be helped.﴾

﴿And follow the best of what has been revealed to you from your Lord⦆ — meaning: the Qur'an, and the entire Qur'an is good. The meaning of the verse is what al-Hasan said: adhere to His obedience and avoid His disobedience, for the Qur'an mentions the ugly so that you avoid it, mentions the lesser so that you do not desire it, and mentions the best so that you prefer it. Al-Suddi said: "The best" is what Allah has commanded in the Book. ﴿Before there comes upon you the punishment suddenly while you do not perceive⦆.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 39, verse 56–61:

﴿Lest a soul should say﴾ means: lest a soul should say. It is like His saying: "And He cast firm mountains upon the earth lest it should shake with you" [al-Nahl: 15], meaning: lest it should shake with you. Al-Mubarrad said: meaning, hasten and beware lest a soul should say. Al-Zajjaj said: for fear that you would come to a state where you say this statement. ﴿Alas for me!﴾ means: alas, my regret! Tahassur (regret) is distress over what has passed. He intended: "yā ḥasratī" (O my regret), in the form of the possessive suffix, but the Arabs convert the first-person possessive yā' into an alif in the invocation (istighātha), so they say: yā ḥasratā [[In "B": yā waylatī.]] and yā nadāmatā (O my remorse). Sometimes they attach a yā' after the alif to indicate the possessive, and likewise Abū Ja'far recited ﴿yā ḥasratāy﴾. It was also said that the meaning of "yā ḥasratā" is: O regret, this is your time. ﴿Over what I neglected concerning Allah's side﴾. Al-Hasan said: I fell short in obedience to Allah. Mujahid said: in the command of Allah. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: in the right of Allah. It was said: I wasted [what was due] in the matter of Allah. It was also said: its meaning is, I fell short in the direction that leads to the pleasure of Allah, and the Arabs call the side (janb) a direction (jānib). ﴿And indeed I was among the mockers﴾, those who ridiculed the religion of Allah, His Book, His Messenger and the believers. Qatadah said: it was not enough for him that he wasted the obedience of Allah, until he began to mock the people of His obedience.

﴿Or say, "Had Allah guided me, I would have been among the God-conscious."﴾ ﴿Or say when he sees the punishment﴾ directly, ﴿"Had I but a return"﴾ a return to the world, ﴿so that I would be among the good-doers﴾, the monotheists.

Then it will be said to this speaker: ﴿"Yes! My verses had certainly come to you, but you denied them and were arrogant, and you were among the disbelievers."﴾ My verses means: the Qur'an. ﴿You denied them﴾ and said that it is not from Allah. ﴿And were arrogant﴾, you were haughty toward belief in them. ﴿And you were among the disbelievers.﴾

﴿And on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied against Allah﴾, claiming that He has a son and a partner, ﴿their faces blackened. Is there not in Hell an abode for the arrogant?﴾ toward belief.

﴿And Allah will save those who feared Him with their triumph﴾. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Abu Bakr recited "bi-mafāzātihim" with an alif, in the plural, meaning: by the ways that lead them to success and salvation. The others recited "bi-mafāzatihim" in the singular, because mafāzah means fawz (triumph), meaning: He saves them by their triumph from the Fire through their good deeds. Al-Mubarrad said: mafāzah is a mafʿalah form from fawz, and its plural is good, like saʿādah and saʿādāt. ﴿No evil will touch them﴾, no harm will befall them, ﴿nor will they grieve.﴾

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 39, verses 62–67:**

﴿Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is, over all things, Guardian.﴾ That is, all things are entrusted to Him, and He is the One who sustains their preservation.

﴿To Him belong the keys (maqalid) of the heavens and the earth.﴾ These are the keys to the treasuries of the heavens and the earth. Its singular is *miqlad*, like *miftah* (key), and *miqlid*, like *mindil* (handkerchief), whose plural is *manadil*. Qatadah and Muqatil said: "The keys of the heavens and the earth are the provision and the mercy." Al-Kalbi said: "They are the treasuries of rain and the treasuries of plants."

﴿And those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah, those are the losers.﴾

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say, "Is it other than Allah that you order me to worship, O ignorant ones?"﴾ Muqatil said: "This was because the disbelievers of Quraysh invited him to the religion of his forefathers." The people of Syria read *ta'murunni* (تَأْمُرُونَنِي) with two light nuns, according to the original form; the people of Medina read it with one light nun, by elision (*hadhf*); and the others read it with one heavy (doubled) nun, by assimilation (*idgham*, merging of the two consonants).

﴿And it has already been revealed to you and to those before you: "If you associate partners with Allah, your deeds will surely be nullified.﴾ The deed you did before the association (of partners). This is addressed to the Messenger (ﷺ), but what is meant is others. It was also said: this is a form of courtesy from Allah, may He be exalted, toward His Prophet, and a warning to others, because Allah had preserved him from associating partners with Him.

﴿And you will surely be among the losers.﴾

﴿Rather, worship Allah alone, and be among the grateful.﴾ For His bounty upon you.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They did not measure Allah with His true measure.﴾ That is, they did not venerate Him with His true veneration when they associated others with Him. Then He informed of His greatness, saying: ﴿The earth entirely will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded in His right hand. Glory be to Him, and high is He above what they associate.﴾

Abdul-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Adam informed us: Shayban informed us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from Ubaydah, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: A rabbi (*hibr*, Jewish scholar) came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Muhammad, we find that Allah places the heavens on one finger, the earths on one finger, the trees on one finger, the water and the moist earth on one finger, and all the rest of creation on one finger, then He says: 'I am the King.'" The Prophet (ﷺ) laughed until his back teeth showed, confirming the rabbi's statement. Then he recited: ﴿They did not measure Allah with His true measure, while the earth entirely will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection.﴾ [Reported by al-Bukhari in the Book of Tafsir, the chapter of Surat al-Zumar, under "They did not measure Allah with His true measure," vol. 8, pp. 550–551.]

Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj narrated it from Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus, from Fudayl ibn Iyad, from Mansur, and he said: "and the mountains and the trees on one finger," and he said: "Then He shakes them, a shaking, and says: 'I am the King, I am Allah.'" [Reported by Muslim in the Book of the Description of the Resurrection, Paradise and Hell, no. 2786, vol. 4, p. 2147.]

Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Shurayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tha'labi informed us: al-Husayn ibn Fanjawayh informed me: Umar ibn al-Khattab informed us: Abdullah ibn al-Fadl informed us: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah informed us: Abu Usamah informed us, from Umar ibn Hamzah, from Salim ibn Abdullah, who said: Abdullah ibn Umar informed me, saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "On the Day of Resurrection Allah will fold up the heavens, then take them in His right hand, then say: 'I am the King; where are the tyrants? Where are the arrogant?' Then He will fold up the earths, then take them in His left hand, then say: 'I am the King; where are the tyrants? Where are the arrogant?'" This is a sound hadith, which Muslim reported from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah. [Reported by Muslim in the Book of the Attributes of the Hypocrites and Their Rulings, no. 2788, vol. 4, p. 2148.]

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tawbah al-Kushmihini informed us: Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Harith informed us: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kisa'i informed us: Abdullah ibn Mahmud informed us: Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Khallal informed us: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Yunus, from al-Zuhri, who said: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab informed me, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "On the Day of Resurrection Allah will seize the earth and fold the heaven in His right hand, then say: 'I am the King; where are the kings of the earth?'" [Reported by al-Bukhari in the Book of Tafsir, the chapter of Surat al-Zumar, under "They did not measure Allah with His true measure," vol. 5, p. 551; by Muslim in the Book of the Description of the Resurrection, Paradise and Hell, no. 2787, vol. 4, p. 2148; and by the author (al-Baghawi) in Sharh al-Sunnah, vol. 15, pp. 110–111.]

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 39, verses 69–71:

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord﴾. "Shone" means "lit up." ﴿With the light of its Lord﴾ means with the light of its Creator. This will be when the Lord manifests Himself to judge between His creatures, so they will not be harmed by His light, just as they are not harmed by the sun on a clear day. Al-Hasan and al-Suddi said: "With the justice of its Lord." By "the earth" they meant the grounds of the Resurrection ('arasat al-qiyamah). ﴿And the Book will be placed﴾, meaning the Book of deeds. ﴿And the prophets and the witnesses will be brought forward﴾. Ibn Abbas said: this refers to those who bear witness for the Messengers that they conveyed the message, and they are the community of Muhammad (ﷺ). Ata said: this refers to the guardian angels (al-hafazah), as indicated by the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And every soul will come, with it a driver and a witness﴾ [Qaf: 21]. ﴿And judgment will be passed between them with truth﴾, meaning with justice. ﴿And they will not be wronged﴾, meaning no addition will be made to their evil deeds and nothing will be subtracted from their good deeds.

﴿And every soul will be paid in full for what it did﴾, meaning the reward for what it did. ﴿And He is most knowing of what they do﴾. Ata said: this means that I know their actions and have no need of a recording scribe or a witness.

﴿And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell﴾ in a harsh driving, ﴿in groups (zumaran)﴾, meaning in companies, one following closely after another, each community separately. Abu Ubayda and al-Akhfash said: "Zumaran" means groups in separate categories; its singular is zumrah.

﴿Until, when they reach it, its gates will be opened﴾, the seven gates, which had been closed before that. The people of Kufa read "futtihat, wa-futihat" (فُتِحَتْ، وَفُتِحَتْ) with a light (single-consonant) form, while the others read them with the intensive form (fattaha, with the doubled consonant), indicating multiplicity. ﴿And its keepers will say to them﴾, as a rebuke and reproach: ﴿Did there not come to you messengers from among you﴾, from your own selves, ﴿reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this your Day?﴾ ﴿They will say: Yes, but the word of punishment has become due against the disbelievers﴾, meaning it was decreed. This is the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind all together" [Hud: 119].

﴿And every soul will be paid in full for what it did﴾, meaning the reward for what it did. ﴿And He is most knowing of what they do﴾. Ata said: this means that I know their actions and have no need of a recording scribe or a witness.

﴿And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell﴾ in a harsh driving, ﴿in groups (zumaran)﴾, meaning in companies, one following closely after another, each community separately. Abu Ubayda and al-Akhfash said: "Zumaran" means groups in separate categories; its singular is zumrah.

﴿Until, when they reach it, its gates will be opened﴾, the seven gates, which had been closed before that. The people of Kufa read "futtihat, wa-futihat" (فُتِحَتْ، وَفُتِحَتْ) with a light (single-consonant) form, while the others read them with the intensive form (fattaha, with the doubled consonant), indicating multiplicity. ﴿And its keepers will say to them﴾, as a rebuke and reproach: ﴿Did there not come to you messengers from among you﴾, from your own selves, ﴿reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this your Day?﴾ ﴿They will say: Yes, but the word of punishment has become due against the disbelievers﴾, meaning it was decreed. This is the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind all together" [Hud: 119].

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 39, verses 72–73:

﴿It will be said: "Enter the gates of Hell, to abide therein forever. Wretched is the abode of the arrogant."﴾ And ﴿those who feared their Lord will be driven to the Garden in groups, until, when they reach it and its gates are opened﴾. The Kufans said: this waw (wa) is extra (za'idah), so that it serves as the response (jawab) to His saying, "until, when they reach it," as in the driving of the disbelievers. This is like Allah the Exalted's saying: ﴿And We gave Moses and Aaron the Criterion and a light﴾ [al-Anbiya': 48] [i.e., a light] [[An addition from "b".]] and the waw is extra.

It was also said: the waw is the waw of the circumstantial clause (wa al-hal). Its meaning is: "and its gates had already been opened," so the waw was introduced to show that they were open before their arrival, while its omission in the first verse shows that they were closed before their arrival.

If the waw in His saying "and its gates are opened" is not taken as extra, the scholars differed regarding the response to His saying, "and its keepers will say to them." The waw there is redundant (mulghah), and its implied sense is: "until, when they reach it and its gates are opened, and its keepers say to them..." Al-Zajjaj said: "In my view, the response is omitted, its implied sense being: 'until, when they reach it and its gates are opened, and its keepers say to them: Peace be upon you, you are good, so enter it, abiding forever,' meaning: they entered it. So 'they entered it' was omitted because the context points to it."

﴿And its keepers will say to them: Peace be upon you, you are good﴾: he means that the keepers of the Garden greet them with peace and say, "You are good." Ibn 'Abbas said: "Good is your station." Qatadah said: when they have crossed the Fire, they are detained upon a bridge between the Garden and the Fire, where some of them take retribution from others; then, when they have been purified and cleansed, they are admitted to the Garden, and Ridwan and his companions say to them, "Peace be upon you, you are good, so enter it, abiding forever." [[See: al-Qurtubi: 15/286.]]

It is narrated from 'Ali, peace be upon him, that he said: "They will be driven to the Garden, and when they reach it they will find at its gate a tree from beneath whose trunk two springs flow. The believer bathes in one of them, and his outward self is purified, and he drinks from the other, and his inward self is purified. The angels will meet them at the gates of the Garden, saying: ﴿Peace be upon you, you are good, so enter it, abiding forever.﴾" [[See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/263; al-Qurtubi: 15/286.]]

And they say, "Praise be to Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us and made us inherit the earth"—that is, the earth of Paradise. "We may settle" (natabawwa'): we may dwell, "in Paradise wherever we will." Allah the Exalted said: "How excellent is the reward of those who work" — the reward of the obedient.

"And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne, glorifying [their Lord] with praise" — that is, encircling and surrounding the Throne, circling around its edges (hawafihi), that is, its sides. "They glorify with the praise of their Lord." It has been said: this is the glorification of delight, not the glorification of worship, because obligation (al-taklif) [[In the manuscript "B": abandoned.]] ceases on that Day. "And it will be judged between them with truth" — that is, judgment will be passed between the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire with justice. "And it will be said, 'Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.'" The people of Paradise say: "Thanks be to Allah," when Allah's promise to them has been fulfilled.
